(WebFetch — CBS News, 24 July 2026)

France/Spain wildfires, 24 July 2026:
- 40,000 people evacuated in south-western France from a fire covering over 25,000 acres.
- French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez called it "the largest fire of the season".
- 80 homes burned, roughly 50 completely destroyed; three firefighters killed.
- Over 10,000 evacuated in the Madrid region, Spain.
- Cap Ferret peninsula: residents fled by boat.
- Le Porge near Bordeaux: resident Patrick Martineau reported flames 500 metres away.
- France invoked the EU civil protection mechanism; EU providing water-bombing planes.
- President Macron warned the crisis remained "very intense".
- Spain declared a state of emergency in the Madrid region.
- Temperatures exceeded 40C (104F); record land burned across the EU in 2026 (second-largest on record).

(Corroborates the brief's wildfire item on Macron's military mobilisation, Spain's national emergency, EU aircraft support, 40C heat and the Cap Ferret evacuation. Evacuation totals vary by outlet and time of day; the brief's 166,000 figure is sourced separately to the Irish Times.)
